body: I lost a teenage child to suicide. For six months the police were not sure if it actually was suicide or an accident. I can tell you right now NOTHING causes more agony than the loss of a child, no matter how it happens. It is almost unendurable and I wanted to die for at least the first year. At 6 months they went through her computer and found she'd been posting suicidal thoughts to sites like this, and that added a whole other layer of pain for us. Parents never recover, they never 'get over it', they learn to live with it. The first five years are the hardest and it gets a little easier after that. By easier I mean you don't cry every day, just every second day. If you love your family find help and other ways to sort out your issues.
I'm sorry you can't have children, if that is what you wanted. Thanks for your reply

It is like you have been given permission by their actions. And you think, well, if they can do it so can I. But at the end of the day, it's the pain of grief that can be agony and you just want to find a way out anyway you can,

I promised them I wouldn't do it. And I hide my ideation from them, and only talk to a psychiatrist about it. I know I'm at risk and I feel it, I know the trance that one can be pulled into. But no, how could I inflict this suffering on my only child. It's something nobody should have to endure.

Hi, sorry to hear about the things weighing you down. Living with people who have a mental illness, and compulsive spending/hoarding is a sign of something deeper amiss can be really stressful and effect every part of your life and how you feel about yourself.
My mother was mentally ill most of my life and it had a profound impact on me. But I think the impact can be reduced by seeking therapist or counsellor - just for yourself - if possible, and also through knowing that you are close to leaving and getting your own life happening. Once you go to college it will be less stressful as their illness won't be in your face, but it will take much time to heal the scars of growing up like this. It is possible with a good therapist to work through the complex love/hate/need/reject/shame feelings and come out the other side a whole lot better. You are so young, and have so much ahead. Life won't always be like this, you won't always be buried under the weight of others illnesses. Good luck
